record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every polygonal billiard table have at least one periodic billiard orbit?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Does every polygon have a periodic orbit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the Euclidean plane (not necessarily convex). Consider the billiard dynamical system inside P: a point particle moves in a straight line at unit speed in the interior of P, and upon reaching a point of the boundary that lies in the relative interior of an edge it reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). Trajectories that hit a vertex of P are considered undefined from that point on. A billiard orbit is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial velocity.

Prove or disprove: every simple polygon P admits at least one periodic billiard orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in full generality. For rational polygons (all angles rational multiples of π), periodic orbits are known to exist and to be dense in phase space via Teichmüller theory. For general polygons the question is open; partial results exist, including the existence of periodic orbits in every acute triangle (Fagnano), every right triangle, and (Schwartz) every obtuse triangle with largest angle less than 100°. The general case, even for arbitrary triangles, remains unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (R. E. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of periodic orbits in general polygons, even triangles, is a well-known open problem; partial progress includes results for rational polygons and triangles with restricted angles.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a periodic billiard orbit in every polygon (even every triangle) is a well-known open problem with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Classical and Open Problems about Billiard Dynamics (O. Knill)
status_evidence.snippet: It is unknown whether every polygon admits a periodic billiard orbit; for rational polygons periodic orbits are dense.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of periodic orbits in arbitrary polygons is listed as an open problem; rational polygons are known to have dense periodic orbits.

status_evidence.title: Periodic billiard orbits in right triangles
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence of periodic orbits in right triangles.
status_evidence.claim: Right triangles are known to admit periodic billiard orbits, contributing to partial progress.
